extras.workflow_content:
name: Deploy to Azure

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-backend
  AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH: './python-backend'
  PYTHON_VERSION: '3.11'
  NODE_VERSION: '20'
  RESOURCE_GROUP: openai-cs-agents-demo-rg
  LOCATION: eastus2
  APP_SERVICE_PLAN: openai-cs-agents-plan
  STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME: openai-cs-agents-frontend

jobs:
  build-and-deploy-backend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: ${{ env.PYTHON_VERSION }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./python-backend
        run: |
          python -m pip install --upgrade pip
          pip install -r requirements.txt

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Resource Group (if not exists)
        run: |
          az group create --name ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} || true

      - name: Create App Service Plan (Free Tier)
        run: |
          az appservice plan create \
            --name ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --sku F1 \
            --is-linux || true

      - name: Create Web App
        run: |
          az webapp create \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --plan ${{ env.APP_SERVICE_PLAN }} \
            --runtime "PYTHON:3.11" || true

      - name: Configure App Settings
        run: |
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings \
              OPENAI_API_KEY="${{ secrets.OPENAI_API_KEY }}" \
              SCM_DO_BUILD_DURING_DEPLOYMENT=true \
              WEBSITES_PORT=8000

      - name: Configure startup command
        run: |
          az webapp config set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --startup-file "gunicorn -w 2 -k uvicorn.workers.UvicornWorker api:app --bind 0.0.0.0:8000"

      - name: Deploy to Azure Web App
        uses: azure/webapps-deploy@v3
        with:
          app-name: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}
          package: ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_PACKAGE_PATH }}

      - name: Output Backend URL
        id: backend-url
        run: |
          BACKEND_URL="https://${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }}.azurewebsites.net"
          echo "BACKEND_URL=$BACKEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT
          echo "Backend deployed to: $BACKEND_URL"

    outputs:
      backend_url: ${{ steps.backend-url.outputs.BACKEND_URL }}

  build-and-deploy-frontend:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: build-and-deploy-backend
    
    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Set up Node.js
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ env.NODE_VERSION }}

      - name: Install pnpm
        run: npm install -g pnpm

      - name: Install dependencies
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm install

      - name: Build frontend
        working-directory: ./ui
        run: pnpm run build
        env:
          NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}

      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Create Static Web App (if not exists)
        run: |
          az staticwebapp create \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --location ${{ env.LOCATION }} \
            --sku Free || true

      - name: Get Static Web App deployment token
        id: swa-token
        run: |
          TOKEN=$(az staticwebapp secrets list \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "properties.apiKey" -o tsv)
          echo "::add-mask::$TOKEN"
          echo "DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN=$TOKEN" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Deploy to Azure Static Web Apps
        uses: Azure/static-web-apps-deploy@v1
        with:
          azure_static_web_apps_api_token: ${{ steps.swa-token.outputs.DEPLOYMENT_TOKEN }}
          repo_token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          action: "upload"
          app_location: "./ui/out"
          output_location: ""
          skip_app_build: true

      - name: Output Frontend URL
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "Frontend deployed to: https://$FRONTEND_URL"

  configure-cors:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [build-and-deploy-backend, build-and-deploy-frontend]
    
    steps:
      - name: Login to Azure
        uses: azure/login@v2
        with:
          creds: ${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}

      - name: Get Static Web App URL
        id: frontend-url
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL=$(az staticwebapp show \
            --name ${{ env.STATIC_WEB_APP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --query "defaultHostname" -o tsv)
          echo "FRONTEND_URL=https://$FRONTEND_URL" >> $GITHUB_OUTPUT

      - name: Configure CORS on Backend
        run: |
          FRONTEND_URL="${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"
          # Pass ALLOWED_ORIGINS to FastAPI's CORSMiddleware via app setting.
          # Do NOT use `az webapp cors add` together with FastAPI's own CORSMiddleware —
          # both would add Access-Control-Allow-Origin headers, causing duplicate-header
          # rejections in browsers.  FastAPI's middleware is the single source of truth.
          az webapp config appsettings set \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --settings ALLOWED_ORIGINS="$FRONTEND_URL,http://localhost:3250,http://localhost:3000"
          # Clear any previously-added Azure-level CORS origins to avoid conflicts.
          az webapp cors remove \
            --name ${{ env.AZURE_WEBAPP_NAME }} \
            --resource-group ${{ env.RESOURCE_GROUP }} \
            --allowed-origins "*" || true

      - name: Summary
        run: |
          echo "=== Deployment Complete ==="
          echo "Backend URL: ${{ needs.build-and-deploy-backend.outputs.backend_url }}"
          echo "Frontend URL: ${{ steps.frontend-url.outputs.FRONTEND_URL }}"

summary.iac_security_summary:
## Security briefing

### 1) Deployment posture
- **Cloud provider:** Azure.
- **Delivery path:** GitHub Actions workflow (`push`, `workflow_dispatch`) on `ubuntu-latest`.
- **Regions / HA / resilience:** No Azure region, availability zone, multi-region, or failover data is present. The provided configuration does **not** show any explicit high-availability or resilience design.

### 2) Secret management
- **Secret store in use:** `github_actions_secret`.
- **Credential handling:** Azure access is supplied via `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}`.
- **Risk posture:** No plaintext secret is shown in the config, but this is still a **static secret-based authentication pattern** stored in GitHub Actions secrets. That increases exposure relative to short-lived federated auth and makes secret rotation operationally important.

### 3) Encryption
- **Encryption-at-rest coverage:** `false` in the aggregate signal.
- **Key management:** No customer-managed key (CMK), key vault integration, or other key lifecycle controls are shown.
- **Implication:** The provided data indicates **missing at-rest encryption coverage** somewhere in the deployment surface; the exact resource(s) are not identified.

### 4) IAM / least-privilege
- **IAM principal:** `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}`.
- **IAM type:** `managed_identity` is stated, but the principal is represented as a GitHub secret. The config therefore shows **credential-based access**, not a clearly defined workload identity flow.
- **Trust relationship:** `github-actions` is trusted.
- **Scope:** `subscription`.
- **Risk posture:** Subscription scope is broad and may exceed least-privilege requirements for an application deployment. No fine-grained role assignments, resource-group scope, or custom role definitions are shown.  
- **OIDC:** `uses_oidc: false`, so the deployment is **not** using GitHub-to-Azure federated identity.

### 5) CI/CD security
- **Runner:** `ubuntu-latest` hosted runner.
- **Trigger surface:** `push` and `workflow_dispatch` increase execution paths; `workflow_dispatch` introduces manual invocation capability.
- **OIDC:** Disabled, so the pipeline relies on a stored secret rather than ephemeral federation.
- **Risk posture:** Hosted runner use is normal, but security depends on workflow hardening, secret handling, and least-privilege credentials. No workflow-level protections, environment gates, or approval controls are shown.

### 6) Container security
- **Not evidenced in provided data.** There are no container/image nodes, so root user settings, health checks, and resource limits cannot be assessed from this configuration.

## Top 3 prioritized actions
1. **Replace `${{ secrets.AZURE_CREDENTIALS }}` with GitHub Actions OIDC federation to Azure** and remove the long-lived secret from workflow dependency.
2. **Reduce IAM scope from subscription-wide to the minimum resource-group/resource scope required** and validate role assignments for least privilege.
3. **Address encryption-at-rest gaps** by identifying the affected Azure resources and enabling storage/database encryption with documented key management controls (preferably CMK where required).

## Component Relationship Graph

- **Entry points:** FastAPI exposes `Login`, `Me`, `Logout`, and `Chat Endpoint`. `Bearer Auth` protects those endpoints plus a `Generic` endpoint.
- **Orchestration:** `OpenAI Agents` can call the `Cancellation`, `FAQ`, `Flight Status`, `Seat Booking`, and `Triage` agents, and can also call tools directly.
- **Agent routing:** `Triage Agent` delegates to `Flight Status Agent` and `FAQ Agent`, but it also directly calls the main tools.
- **Model usage:** All listed agents use `gpt-4.1-mini`. Both guardrails also use `gpt-4.1-mini`.
- **Tool access:** Multiple agents have broad tool reach. For example, `Cancellation`, `FAQ`, `Flight Status`, `Seat Booking`, and `Triage` can all call tools such as `Baggage`, `Cancel Flight`, `Display Seat Map`, `Faq Lookup`, and `Flight Status`.
- **Direct framework tool access:** `OpenAI Agents` can call `Lookup Reservation` and `Update Seat` directly, even though no agent is shown using them.
- **Guardrails:** `Relevance Guardrail` and `Jailbreak Guardrail` are present, but the graph shows no direct connections to specific agents or tools.
- **Datastores:** `Sqlite` is present with **no connections shown**, so no datastore access is visible in the graph.
